newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Britain's Hambros kicks off S.Africa fund.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Hambros kicks off S.Africa fund.

text.p: Britain's Hambros Plc said on Wednesday that it had launched a private equity fund with commitments of 200 million rand to invest in South African companies.

Hambro Private Equity Investors (HPEI) will invest in medium and larger-sized firms with a total value of upwards of 50 million rand offering a minimum equity participation of 25 million rand. The fund will be advised by Hambro Private Equity SA Ltd (HPE).
Investors in the fund include Anglo American Corp Pension Fund, De Beers Pension Fund, Eskom Pension & Provident Fund and Genbel Securities Ltd.
"The support of the blue chip group of South African and international investors that we have assembled is significant in the development of a new asset class," said HPE chairman Tony Williamson.
He added that the fund would differ from local rivals through its syndication structure and would access investors' funds on a deal by deal basis.
There is currently estimated to be about four billion rand of dedicated private equity funds invested or available to be invested in South Africa.
This is expected to grow as unbundling of the country's conglomerates continues and the process of black economic empowerment takes hold.

HPE director Partrick Maxwell said he expected the size of private equity deals to increase in South Africa. "This would mirror the development of the mature private equity market places of the United States and the UK," he said.
Maxwell said Hambros would focus on established businesses in sectors including mining, high technology, property and financial services.
